pages.text: Sunlight brings about 1000 W/m² at noon, less as the Sun sinks. Concentrated C times and let through a shutter of opening g, it heats the target until it radiates away what it absorbs: αgCG = εσT⁴. The target's temperature decides what melts - and what boils off.
$(thing)Set$(): Concentration C, Shutter opening g.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Thin cloud: the sunlight varies by ±3%·d.

$(thing)Limits$(): The Sun is too low (or down); Something shades the mirrors; Overcast: no sunlight to concentrate; The crucible is melting (above 3,200 K).$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): The hotter above its melting point, the faster the charge melts.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Sunlight: G = 1000·sin(elevation)$(br)Flux on target: q = g·C·G$(br)Target temperature: T = (αq/εσ + T_amb⁴)^(1/4)$(br)Above the melting point: T − T_m
